sara (ml-eng): Heads up — after HF->Redwood conversion of mosaic-8k-quant I'm seeing BOS/EOS/PAD ids drift relative to what HF reported. Chats drop the initial system message sometimes. Anyone seen this pattern?

dan (tokenizer): Can you paste the added_tokens.json and the tokenizer config.json you used for conversion? Also quick outputs for tokenizer.special_tokens_map and vocab_size.

sara (ml-eng): Sure, minimal artifacts below. Conversion was via our hf-to-redwood script with --preserve-added-tokens toggled on.

```json
// added_tokens.json (from the repo)
["<bos>", "<eos>", "<pad>", "<sep>", "<role_user>", "<role_assistant>"]
```

```json
// tokenizer_config.json (excerpt)
{
  "bos_token": "<bos>",
  "eos_token": "<eos>",
  "pad_token": "<pad>",
  "unk_token": "<unk>",
  "added_tokens": ["<role_user>", "<role_assistant>"]
}
```

nina (runtime): Quick note: HF converters sometimes append added tokens when merging tokenizers or vocab files; order can differ and HF's internal added_tokens_encoder might assign ids at runtime. If conversion doesn't pin ids, Redwood import can assign the next free ids which causes shift.

mike (oncall): I ran into something similar last month where pad_token was unset in the config and during quantize we ended up with pad mapped to id 1 (reserved) while HF expected pad id 0. That off-by-one cascaded into chat templates that assume <bos>=2.

sara (ml-eng): Here are the outputs from the tokenizer after conversion (redwood side):

```
vocab_size: 50256
special_tokens_map: {"<unk>": 0, "<pad>": 1, "<bos>": 3, "<eos>": 4}
added_tokens_count: 6
```

sara (ml-eng): HF original had <bos>=2, <eos>=3, <pad>=0. So we have a mismatch.

dan (tokenizer): @sara this matches the theory. Two quick remediation paths: (1) during conversion persist explicit id mapping by creating an additions.json that includes id assignments, or (2) remap special token ids in Redwood's tokenizer object post-import to match HF expectations.

dan (tokenizer): Short python snippet to enforce mapping after load:

```python
# after tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(redwood_path)
explicit_map = {"<bos>": 2, "<eos>": 3, "<pad>": 0}
for tkn, idx in explicit_map.items():
    tokenizer.add_special_tokens({tkn: tkn})
    tokenizer._convert_added_token_to_id(tkn)  # internal API varies by HF version
# OR directly set tokenizer.special_tokens_map[token_name] = idx and save
```

nina (runtime): Also add an assert in our conversion CI: token_id(token) == expected_id for the small set of reserved tokens. If assertion fails, fail the import and emit a diff patch with mapping. That prevents silent shifts.

convert-bot: import-job-4821 completed for model mosaic-8k-quant. Warnings: reserved index collision: PAD collides with existing id 1; 4 added tokens appended at end.

mike (oncall): Another wrinkle: quant pipeline packs kv cache indices; if we change ids post-quantization we must re-run quantize step. Otherwise stored indices in weights/meta may be inconsistent with on-disk tokenizer ids.

sara (ml-eng): Good catch — so plan: 1) roll back the converted artifact and pin tokenizer ids to HF mapping, 2) re-run quantization, 3) run regression eval (chat templates + unit prompt set) to validate. I'll open a tiny PR to the conversion script to export an explicit additions.json with id assignments.

dan (tokenizer): I can add the CI check and a small tool to diff hf tokenizer vs imported tokenizer and auto-generate a remap patch.

nina (runtime): I'll add a runtime guard that refuses to serve a model if special token id assertions fail for the deployed chat template. Fail fast.

mike (oncall): Ping me when you re-quantize; I'll watch infra for perf regressions.

sara (ml-eng): Thanks all :thumbsup: I'll attach the repro artifacts in the PR and tag you.
